{{Short description|Generalization of closed graph, open mapping, and uniform boundedness theorem}}
In mathematics, particularly in [[functional analysis]] and [[convex analysis]], the '''Ursescu theorem''' is a theorem that generalizes the [[Closed graph theorem (functional analysis)|closed graph theorem]], the [[Open mapping theorem (functional analysis)|open mapping theorem]], and the [[uniform boundedness principle]].

== Ursescu theorem ==

The following notation and notions are used, where <math>\mathcal{R} : X \rightrightarrows Y</math> is a [[set-valued function]] and <math>S</math> is a non-empty subset of a [[topological vector space]] <math>X</math>:
* the [[affine span]] of <math>S</math> is denoted by <math>\operatorname{aff} S</math> and the [[linear span]] is denoted by <math>\operatorname{span} S.</math>
* <math>S^{i} := \operatorname{aint}_X S</math> denotes the [[algebraic interior]] of <math>S</math> in <math>X.</math>
* <math>{}^{i}S:= \operatorname{aint}_{\operatorname{aff}(S - S)} S</math> denotes the [[Algebraic interior#Relative algebraic interior|relative algebraic interior]] of <math>S</math> (i.e. the algebraic interior of <math>S</math> in <math>\operatorname{aff}(S - S)</math>).
* <math>{}^{ib}S := {}^{i}S</math> if <math>\operatorname{span} \left(S - s_0\right)</math> is [[Barrelled space|barreled]] for some/every <math>s_0 \in S</math> while <math>{}^{ib}S := \varnothing</math> otherwise.
** If <math>S</math> is convex then it can be shown that for any <math>x \in X,</math> <math>x \in {}^{ib} S</math> if and only if the cone generated by <math>S - x</math> is a barreled linear subspace of <math>X</math> or equivalently, if and only if <math>\cup_{n \in \N} n (S - x)</math> is a barreled linear subspace of <math>X</math>
* The '''domain of <math>\mathcal{R}</math>''' is <math>\operatorname{Dom} \mathcal{R} := \{ x \in X : \mathcal{R}(x) \neq \varnothing \}.</math>
* The '''image of <math>\mathcal{R}</math>''' is <math>\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R} := \cup_{x \in X} \mathcal{R}(x).</math> For any subset <math>A \subseteq X,</math> <math>\mathcal{R}(A) := \cup_{x \in A} \mathcal{R}(x).</math>
* The '''graph of <math>\mathcal{R}</math>''' is <math>\operatorname{gr} \mathcal{R} := \{ (x, y) \in X \times Y : y \in \mathcal{R}(x) \}.</math>
* <math>\mathcal{R}</math> is '''closed''' (respectively, '''convex''') if the graph of <math>\mathcal{R}</math> is closed (resp. convex) in <math>X \times Y.</math>
** Note that <math>\mathcal{R}</math> is convex if and only if for all <math>x_0, x_1 \in X</math> and all <math>r \in [0, 1],</math> <math>r \mathcal{R}\left(x_0\right) + (1 - r) \mathcal{R}\left(x_1\right) \subseteq \mathcal{R} \left(r x_0 + (1 - r) x_1\right).</math>
* The '''inverse of <math>\mathcal{R}</math>''' is the set-valued function <math>\mathcal{R}^{-1} : Y \rightrightarrows X</math> defined by <math>\mathcal{R}^{-1}(y) := \{ x \in X : y \in \mathcal{R}(x) \}.</math> For any subset <math>B \subseteq Y,</math> <math>\mathcal{R}^{-1}(B) := \cup_{y \in B} \mathcal{R}^{-1}(y).</math>
** If <math>f : X \to Y</math> is a function, then its inverse is the set-valued function <math>f^{-1} : Y \rightrightarrows X</math> obtained from canonically identifying <math>f</math> with the set-valued function <math>f : X \rightrightarrows Y</math> defined by <math>x \mapsto \{ f(x)\}.</math>
* <math>\operatorname{int}_T S</math> is the [[Interior (topology)|topological interior]] of <math>S</math> with respect to <math>T,</math> where <math>S \subseteq T.</math>
* <math>\operatorname{rint} S := \operatorname{int}_{\operatorname{aff} S} S</math> is the [[Interior (topology)|interior]] of <math>S</math> with respect to <math>\operatorname{aff} S.</math>

=== Statement ===

{{Math theorem|name=Theorem{{sfn|Zălinescu|2002|p=23}}|note='''Ursescu'''|math_statement=
Let <math>X</math> be a [[Complete topological vector space|complete]] [[Metrizable topological vector space|semi-metrizable]] [[Locally convex topological vector space|locally convex]] [[topological vector space]] and <math>\mathcal{R} : X \rightrightarrows Y</math> be a [[Closed (mathematics)|closed]] [[Convex function|convex]] multifunction with non-empty domain. 
Assume that <math>\operatorname{span} (\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R} - y)</math> is a [[barrelled space]] for some/every <math>y \in \operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R}.</math> 
Assume that <math>y_0 \in {}^{i}(\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R})</math> and let <math>x_0 \in \mathcal{R}^{-1}\left(y_0\right)</math> (so that <math>y_0 \in \mathcal{R}\left(x_0\right)</math>). 
Then for every neighborhood <math>U</math> of <math>x_0</math> in <math>X,</math> <math>y_0</math> belongs to the relative interior of <math>\mathcal{R}(U)</math> in <math>\operatorname{aff} (\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R})</math> (that is, <math>y_0 \in \operatorname{int}_{\operatorname{aff} (\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R})} \mathcal{R}(U)</math>). 
In particular, if <math>{}^{ib}(\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R}) \neq \varnothing</math> then <math>{}^{ib}(\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R}) = {}^{i}(\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R}) = \operatorname{rint} (\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R}).</math>
}}

== Corollaries ==

=== Closed graph theorem ===

{{Math theorem|name=[[Closed graph theorem]] |math_statement=
Let <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math> be [[Fréchet space]]s and <math>T : X \to Y</math> be a linear map. Then <math>T</math> is continuous if and only if the graph of <math>T</math> is closed in <math>X \times Y.</math>
}}

{{math proof|
For the non-trivial direction, assume that the graph of <math>T</math> is closed and let <math>\mathcal{R} := T^{-1} : Y \rightrightarrows X.</math> It is easy to see that <math>\operatorname{gr} \mathcal{R}</math> is closed and convex and that its image is <math>X.</math> 
Given <math>x \in X,</math> <math>(Tx, x)</math> belongs to <math>Y \times X</math> so that for every open neighborhood <math>V</math> of <math>Tx</math> in <math>Y,</math> <math>\mathcal{R}(V) = T^{-1}(V)</math> is a neighborhood of <math>x</math> in <math>X.</math> 
Thus <math>T</math> is continuous at <math>x.</math> 
[[Q.E.D.]]
}}

=== Uniform boundedness principle ===

{{Math theorem|name=[[Uniform boundedness principle]]|math_statement=
Let <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math> be [[Fréchet space]]s and <math>T : X \to Y</math> be a bijective linear map. Then <math>T</math> is continuous if and only if <math>T^{-1} : Y \to X</math> is continuous. Furthermore, if <math>T</math> is continuous then <math>T</math> is an isomorphism of [[Fréchet space]]s.
}}

{{math proof|Apply the closed graph theorem to <math>T</math> and <math>T^{-1}.</math> 
Q.E.D.}}

=== Open mapping theorem ===

{{Math theorem|name=[[Open mapping theorem (functional analysis)|Open mapping theorem]] |math_statement=
Let <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math> be [[Fréchet space]]s and <math>T : X \to Y</math> be a continuous surjective linear map. Then T is an [[open map]].
}}

{{math proof|
Clearly, <math>T</math> is a closed and convex relation whose image is <math>Y.</math> 
Let <math>U</math> be a non-empty open subset of <math>X,</math> let <math>y</math> be in <math>T(U),</math> and let <math>x</math> in <math>U</math> be such that <math>y = Tx.</math> 
From the Ursescu theorem it follows that <math>T(U)</math> is a neighborhood of <math>y.</math> Q.E.D.}}

=== Additional corollaries ===

The following notation and notions are used for these corollaries, where <math>\mathcal{R} : X \rightrightarrows Y</math> is a set-valued function, <math>S</math> is a non-empty subset of a [[topological vector space]] <math>X</math>:
* a '''[[convex series]] with elements of <math>S</math>''' is a [[Series (mathematics)|series]] of the form <math display="inline">\sum_{i=1}^\infty r_i s_i</math> where all <math>s_i \in S</math> and <math display="inline">\sum_{i=1}^\infty r_i = 1</math> is a series of non-negative numbers. If <math display="inline">\sum_{i=1}^\infty r_i s_i</math> converges then the series is called '''convergent''' while if <math>\left(s_i\right)_{i=1}^{\infty}</math> is bounded then the series is called '''bounded''' and '''b-convex'''.
* <math>S</math> is '''ideally convex''' if any convergent b-convex series of elements of <math>S</math> has its sum in <math>S.</math>
* <math>S</math> is '''lower ideally convex''' if there exists a [[Fréchet space]] <math>Y</math> such that <math>S</math> is equal to the projection onto <math>X</math> of some ideally convex subset ''B'' of <math>X \times Y.</math> Every ideally convex set is lower ideally convex.

{{Math theorem |name=Corollary |math_statement=
Let <math>X</math> be a barreled [[first countable space]] and let <math>C</math> be a subset of <math>X.</math> Then:
# If <math>C</math> is lower ideally convex then <math>C^{i} = \operatorname{int} C.</math>
# If <math>C</math> is ideally convex then <math>C^{i} = \operatorname{int} C = \operatorname{int} \left(\operatorname{cl} C\right) = \left(\operatorname{cl} C\right)^i.</math>
}}

== Related theorems ==

=== Simons' theorem ===

{{Math theorem|name=[[Jim Simons|Simons']] theorem{{sfn|Zălinescu|2002|p=22-23}}|note=|math_statement=
Let <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math> be [[first countable]] with <math>X</math> locally convex. Suppose that <math>\mathcal{R} : X \rightrightarrows Y</math> is a multimap with non-empty domain that satisfies [[Convex series#Conditions (Hx) and (Hwx)|condition (Hw''x'')]] or else assume that <math>X</math> is a [[Fréchet space]] and that <math>\mathcal{R}</math> is [[Convex series#Types of subsets|lower ideally convex]]. 
Assume that <math>\operatorname{span} (\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R} - y)</math> is [[Barrelled space|barreled]] for some/every <math>y \in \operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R}.</math> 
Assume that <math>y_0 \in {}^{i}(\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R})</math> and let <math>x_0 \in \mathcal{R}^{-1}\left(y_0\right).</math> 
Then for every neighborhood <math>U</math> of <math>x_0</math> in <math>X,</math> <math>y_0</math> belongs to the relative interior of <math>\mathcal{R}(U)</math> in <math>\operatorname{aff} (\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R})</math> (i.e. <math>y_0 \in \operatorname{int}_{\operatorname{aff} (\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R})} \mathcal{R}(U)</math>). 
In particular, if <math>{}^{ib}(\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R}) \neq \varnothing</math> then <math>{}^{ib}(\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R}) = {}^{i}(\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R}) = \operatorname{rint} (\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R}).</math>
}}

=== Robinson–Ursescu theorem ===

The implication (1) <math>\implies</math> (2) in the following theorem is known as the Robinson–Ursescu theorem.{{sfn|Zălinescu|2002|p=24}} 

{{Math theorem|name=Robinson–Ursescu theorem{{sfn|Zălinescu|2002|p=24}} |note=|math_statement=
Let <math>(X, \|\,\cdot\,\|)</math> and <math>(Y, \|\,\cdot\,\|)</math> be [[normed space]]s and <math>\mathcal{R} : X \rightrightarrows Y</math> be a multimap with non-empty domain. 
Suppose that <math>Y</math> is a [[barreled space]], the graph of <math>\mathcal{R}</math> verifies condition [[Convex series#Conditions (Hx) and (Hwx)|condition (Hw''x'')]], and that <math>(x_0, y_0) \in \operatorname{gr} \mathcal{R}.</math> 
Let <math>C_X</math> (resp. <math>C_Y</math>) denote the closed unit ball in <math>X</math> (resp. <math>Y</math>) (so <math>C_X = \{ x \in X : \| x \| \leq 1 \}</math>). 
Then the following are equivalent:
# <math>y_0</math> belongs to the [[algebraic interior]] of <math>\operatorname{Im} \mathcal{R}.</math> 
# <math>y_0 \in \operatorname{int} \mathcal{R}\left(x_0 + C_X\right).</math> 
# There exists <math>B > 0</math> such that for all <math>0 \leq r \leq 1,</math> <math>y_0 + B r C_Y \subseteq \mathcal{R} \left(x_0 + r C_X\right).</math> 
# There exist <math>A > 0</math> and <math>B > 0</math> such that for all <math>x \in x_0 + A C_X</math> and all <math>y \in y_0 + A C_Y,</math> <math>d\left(x, \mathcal{R}^{-1}(y)\right) \leq B \cdot d(y, \mathcal{R}(x)).</math> 
# There exists <math>B > 0</math> such that for all <math>x \in X</math> and all <math>y \in y_0 + B C_Y,</math> <math>d \left(x, \mathcal{R}^{-1}(y)\right) \leq \frac{1 + \left\|x - x_0\right\|}{B - \left\|y - y_0\right\|} \cdot d(y, \mathcal{R}(x)).</math>
}}
